raw_response:
I am getting old now, and with only 4.1 mu and just myself at home, I will not do anything fancy this year. I will still follow the usual wheat-maize rotation because it is the safest for me. Wheat and maize together keep the land busy all year, and even if one side is not so good, the other can still help. I only finished primary school, so I mostly farm by what I have seen over the years and what the neighbors do. Last year the wheat did better when I put a base fertilizer and then a second urea topdress, so I will do that again. But I cannot spend too much at once, so I will keep the rate in the middle, not the highest. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate at the key times, not too many times. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is short, so I will harvest wheat and plant maize right away with simple land preparation or direct seeding if I can get help from a machine. I want steady grain, not taking risks.
